title: Find which push keeps raising the stray-branch ask, and make it name its destination
why: Owner ask ask-mw8321blnx (11:05 CST Nov 8): the push-stray-branch ask reached him on "Push the merged lane head", and he asks why it keeps coming up in the past 36 h. Decision plain-push-asks (rulings 206 a and 207 a, 2026-11-03) asks on an implied push (`git push origin HEAD`, a bare push) whose name differs from the branch's upstream; an explicit `HEAD:<branch>` is silent. The rate and the sessions are unmeasured: guard.log on the Mac holds them.
note: Coordinator 11:07 CST Nov 8: sent to lane push-head-upstream-name. Not new: push-stray-branch has been on main since item 206 a (Nov 3); #1814 changed no guard. The lane's likely cause, unmeasured until it sees the command: it asks when the destination differs from the upstream even when that destination is the lane's existing PR branch. Planned fix, red first: ask only when the destination does not exist on the remote yet. The ask text holds only the description "Push the merged lane head" and rule id push-stray-branch; no command or session. Narrowing changes what decision plain-push-asks says ruling 206 a asks on, so the record edit needs the owner's word (outcomes-stale-decision-protocol). Page item 432 (11:10 CST Nov 8): skip the prompt when the branch already exists on the remote (pick a), or keep it and fix the remedy only (b). Measured by the lane: `lane-x` tracking `origin/batch-1` asks on `git push origin HEAD` whether or not origin/lane-x exists. The lane holds the fix until the answer. Item 432 re-marked 11:14 CST Nov 8 at the lane's word: option a widens the shared push guard, so it carries the ruling line and widens:true; pick is b (remedy names HEAD:<branch>). Owner item 432 a (page answer 17:49Z = 11:49 CST Nov 8): skip the ask when the branch already exists on GitHub; it narrows 206 a. His note: "shouldn't it stay quiet rergardless?" Triage replied that quiet regardless would drop the new-branch ask 206 a guards; a new question if he wants it. Routed to lane push-head-upstream-name (session_013NEJL1YxsYqim39RK6JeZP), whose decision record is the home. Lane 13:39 CST Nov 8: #2228 has its cost row at a0d5d904b; records next; it waits for #2199's final head. Owner ask ask-mw8j7h8qhn (page, 18:37 CST Nov 8): the push-stray-branch ask fired again on a push he believes was correct. Find the push (command, local branch, its upstream, destination) in the session that raised it or the push-stray-branch lines of ~/.claude/state/guard.log on the machine that ran it; judge it against plain-push-asks' table and Silent list. If a false alarm: a red test in hooks/test_guard.py replaying the case, a guard fix that silences it while the 2026-11-03 mylocal -> origin/lane/x case still asks, and the decision's Silent list updated, in a lane with review. If the ask was right, say so and stop. Report at most 10 lines: the command, false alarm or not, the PR. Triage's container has no guard.log (it restarted at 18:09 CST) and none of triage's own pushes raised the ask. Owner item 432 a (skip when the branch exists on GitHub) may already cover it once #2327 lands. Lane report on ask-mw8j7h8qhn (18:43 CST Nov 8): not a false alarm. Lane lane-step-dup-check (session_013NEJL2hXLvodLuczRGgNHP), builder agent at 18:28 CST, ran a chained `git push origin lane-step-dup-check-build4` (implied destination, name not on origin), which made stray branch origin/lane-step-dup-check-build4 when run alone at 18:32 CST; the explicit `src:lane-step-dup-check-build` push was silent per the Silent list. Ruling 206 a asks on exactly this; item 432 a (#2327) keeps asking for a branch new on the remote. No PR. Caveat: the branch's upstream is not in the transcript.
